summary: RACI answers who does what for each WBS task. WBS is the foundation: every level-3 work package has a unique wbs_code that threads through RACI (rows), RAID (wbs_links), and the status report. Column headers are derived dynamically from distinct WBS owner values; rows are WBS tasks.
generation_rules: Root JSON: {"roles": [ /* distinct WBS owner strings */ ], "rows": [ /* one per WBS task */ ]}.
Set `roles` to every distinct non-empty `owner` value from the WBS work_packages (first-seen order). Do not add columns that are not WBS owners.
Each row object: wbs_code (string, required), activity (string), assignments (object mapping WBS owner name to R, A, C, or I).
Include one RACI row per level-3 WBS work package; wbs_code must exactly match the WBS.
Set activity to the WBS element title (optionally prefixed with the wbs_code for readability).
Every role in `roles` must appear as a key in each row's assignments.
Each row must have exactly one Accountable (A) assignment.
The WBS owner for each task must hold R (Responsible — holds the pen) or A (Accountable) in that row.
Use R for who performs the work; A for who owns delivery; C for parties consulted; I for parties informed.
